interpretationNotes: Fiscal 2026 ended Jan 31, 2026. Filer is Marvell Technology, Inc. (Delaware, CIK 1835632; the former Bermuda parent Marvell Technology Group Ltd is CIK 1058057). Balance sheet and share count EXCLUDE the Celestial AI (closed 2026-02-02, cash ~$1.3B + ~24.5M shares + earnout) and XConn (closed 2026-02-10, ~$280M cash + ~2.1M shares) acquisitions and the NVIDIA Series A preferred (2026-03-31) because all occurred after the balance-sheet date (10-K Note 16 Subsequent Events); the Celestial earnout is therefore not a Jan-31 claim. No stock options table is disclosed in the 10-K (options null). Technology license obligations (about $244.5M at Jan 31: current $84.1M + non-current $160.4M, Note 15 of 10-Q comparative) are not included in debt. Customer warrant fair values shown are grant-date values; the FY2025 and FY2026 warrants total up to 5.2M shares.
Fiscal year ends on the Saturday nearest January 31. FY2026 = year ended 2026-01-31. TTM runs to the Q2 FY2027 quarter end 2026-08-01.
Reviewed package (dist/data/incremental-MRVL-2026-10-18-v3) figures for the Aug-1 balance sheet and Aug-18 capital were re-checked against the 10-Q and the Aug-19 8-K exhibit and agree.
Annual and TTM balance sheets are not comparable for capital: Celestial, XConn, NVIDIA preferred and Google warrant all fall between the two dates.
No convertible notes or capped calls exist at either date; debt is senior unsecured notes only.

interpretationNotes: Fiscal year ended July 3, 2026 (53 weeks), audited 10-K filed 2026-08-17. Statements are filed in whole USD millions (no decimals). No debt: the $2.0B term loan (issued at the Feb 2025 spin-off from Western Digital) was settled in full on March 4, 2026 and the $1.5B revolver is undrawn. No options, no warrants, no convertibles; the only employee claims are RSUs/PSUs (6.6M; PSU max-case adds ~2.2M more shares) and ESPP purchase rights ($71M unamortized). Share count: filed balance sheet is rounded to 146 million; the exact 146,419,001 is the Aug 7, 2026 cover figure (carried only because the period-end exact count is not disclosed); company repurchased ~3M shares ($4.5B) in FY26 and announced a $14.0B program on Aug 5, 2026, so shares may be lower after Aug 7. Spin-off items: Western Digital has almost exited its stake (80.1% distributed Feb 21, 2025; 14.6% disposed June 9, 2025 and 5.8M shares on Feb 18, 2026 via debt-for-equity exchanges; WDC retained 1,691,884 shares (about 1.2%) after Feb 18, 2026 and expects to monetize the rest by end of 2026 (these are already inside the outstanding share count, so no extra dilution); the $128M tax indemnification liability is recorded; Tax Matters Agreement restricts share issuances/business combinations. Items NOT counted in the numeric fields: Flash Ventures notes receivable and equity investments $679M (operating JV supply arrangement; balance sheet shows $678M), 20% SDSS equity-method stake $167M, Unis Venture 48% (not material), Flash Ventures lease guarantees $923M (contingent), unrecognized tax benefits $323M plus $16M interest/penalties, income tax payable current $1,286M, customer refund liabilities (security deposits) $1,500M and contract liabilities $849M current + $393M non-current (customer prepayments under long-term agreements), long-term supplier commitments $5,892M. After year end: two new long-term customer agreements totaling $31.3B.
Spun off from Western Digital on Feb 21, 2025; fiscal year ends the Friday closest to June 30 (FY2026 ended July 3, 2026).
Annual and TTM bases are identical because no 10-Q for fiscal Q1 FY2027 (quarter ending about Oct 2, 2026) had been filed by 2026-10-20.
Values cross-checked against XBRL company facts (revenue 20,248; operating income 12,389; cash 4,762; lease liability 201; cover shares 146,419,001) - all match.
FY2026 reported figures reflect an extreme pricing cycle (revenue +175% to $20.2B, operating margin 61%); also includes $808M gain on Nanya securities below operating income.

interpretationNotes: Balance sheet, H1 2026 and H1 2025 flows come from the Q2 2026 6-K (Exhibit 99.1, TIFRS-basis, reviewed not audited); the 6-K main document is a cover page (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526322030/2026q2_quarterly_reports.htm), the statements are in Exhibit 99.1. FY2025 annual flows come directly from the TIFRS annual report (6-K 0001193125-26-068366, Feb 25 2026, Exhibit 99.1); all three TTM flow components are TIFRS. The separate annual-reference base and annual history remain IASB IFRS. Basis difference: the 20-F balance sheet uses IASB IFRS (UMC shares held by associates treated as treasury stock, lower equity-method carrying), the 6-K uses TIFRS; this affects equity-method carrying (June 30 2026 NT$96,474,468 thousand includes Hsun Chieh at NT$34,229,937 thousand vs NT$12,792,773 thousand at Dec 31 2025 per Q2 6-K Note 6(7)) and equity, not revenue or operating income. H1 2026 includes non-operating gains of NT$26.4bn from associates and NT$8.2bn FVTPL gains, all below operating income and excluded here. Debt excludes IFRS 16 leases (operatingLeaseLiabilities), excludes guarantee deposits (customer capacity deposits NT$40,045,045 thousand, Note 6(28)) and excludes the declared dividend (shown in otherClaims). Treasury shares (30.551 million) are excluded from sharesOutstanding. UMC has no stock options or warrants; restricted stock awards are issued shares already counted. The exchangeable bonds convert into NOVATEK shares held by UMC and matured 2026-07-07 (after period end). ADS ratio: one ADS = five ordinary shares (Note 6(19)a(ii), 20-F cover); 147 million ADSs outstanding at Jun 30 2026.
All amounts are NT$ millions (statements are in NT$ thousands); share counts in millions of ordinary shares; per-ADS value = per-ordinary-share value x 5.

Annual snapshot is from the IASB-basis 20-F; TTM balance sheet is from the TIFRS-basis 6-K; see snapshot notes for the equity-method/treasury-stock basis difference. Revenue and operating income agree on both bases.
Latest filed interim before 2026-10-20 is the Q2 2026 six-month report (6-K filed 2026-07-29); Q3 2026 statements are not yet filed.

The June corporate financing bridge adds $1,757 million of assumed retained proceeds: $2,200 million issued, less $30 million issuance costs, $123 million capped-call premium and $290 million concurrent buyback. Cash is fungible; this is an allocation assumption, not an identified bank balance.

reviewRequired: The model uses the issuer-reconciled fee revenue, including its share of equity-method fee businesses. Common pretax earnings equal fee-related earnings attributable to BAM plus investment and other income net of interest. Subtracting cash taxes gives distributable earnings less the stock-compensation addback. All post-reorganization common shares are included; BN ownership and minority interests are not deducted again.

Owner earnings already include financing costs and proportionate ownership. The model does not add all investments or cash, or subtract consolidated-fund debt and minority interests a second time. Investments whose earnings are included receive no separate asset-value addback.

The denominator includes all outstanding BAM common shares after the reorganization, excluding treasury shares. Brookfield Corporation’s ownership of BAM is not another minority-interest deduction. Options on Brookfield Corporation are a different issuer’s shares and are not added to BAM.

The annual 16.3 million incremental diluted-EPS shares serve as a proxy for combined option and escrow dilution, not a reported period-end award count. Zero to twice this proxy tests an effect of roughly 1% on value per share. No separate option-value deduction is applied. Already-issued restricted stock and escrow-share cancellations must not be double counted.

Owner earnings retain stock-compensation costs and already reflect attributable ownership and financing costs. Consolidated fund assets, fund borrowings and minority interests are not added or deducted a second time.

The forecast assumes that each dollar of new required common equity supports $3 of fee revenue. The terminal 25% return applies to new incremental equity, not the entire existing book-equity balance. This lower terminal capital efficiency raises required retention; it does not assume an unfunded jump in the existing capital stock.

Fee revenue and owner earnings are reconciled non-GAAP business measures. The 2022 predecessor year is contextual because the reorganization and bundled compensation addback limit comparability; the 2023–2025 owner-earnings series is directly reconciled.
interpretationNotes: BAM is the asset manager, not Brookfield Corporation. February2025 reorganization presents full manager ownership with approximately1.6billion total issuer shares. Use attributable fee-business equity model and avoid subtracting consolidated fund/NCI claims twice. GAAP revenue includes volatile unrealized carry; model fee revenue and common pretax earnings are explicitly reconciled in additions/BAM.json. Debt maturity and operating lease splits are unclassified/undisclosed; model does not require a fictitious EV bridge.
2025reverseacquisition uses fullmanager comparative2023–2025; do not splice old27%-owned shell or BrookfieldCorporation history.

Preferred principal is replaced with maximum mandatory-conversion dilution plus separate remaining-dividend PV. Fixed claims include NCI, net pension and the separately flagged supplier-financing proxy. Employee option tranches retain 5m vested and 15m expected-to-vest counts; the remaining 1m not-expected-to-vest is conservatively included at an $184.88 inferred strike and a 5-year life.

The default keeps recent AI buildout intensity in the explicit forecast: sales-to-new-capital of 0.22 means about $4.55 of net reinvestment per $1 of incremental revenue. With current debt and other claims, this scenario produces negative modeled common equity, displayed at a zero floor. It is a conservative conditional scenario, not an assertion that Oracle is worthless. Post-buildout capital efficiency, customer funding and terminal assumptions materially change the result; historical book capital is contextual and is not substituted for future investment.
August 2026 restricted cash of $2,565m is excluded from excess cash. The 141m ATM shares and $19.9bn net proceeds are already in the August balance sheet and are not added again.

Short-term capex financing has no standalone reported closing balance. A conservative claim proxy assumes zero opening at FY2024 and accumulates net financing of $1,422m + $3,345m = $4,767m for May 2026 and subtracts $830m to reach $3,937m for August. The notes-payable schedule reconciles separately and excludes these cash flows. An omitted $1bn opening balance would reduce value by about $0.33/share; the full proxy is about $1.3–1.6/share.

The 31.238285m maximum mandatory preferred-conversion shares are an explicit conservative current-value proxy for a future market-price collar; the minimum 24.99063m sensitivity is available. Preferred carrying amount of $4,954m is not also subtracted. Remaining cumulative dividends are discounted separately at a 6.5% analyst rate; nominal payments provide a sensitivity.

Annual 81m restricted awards and 21m options are carried into August because no complete interim rollforward is disclosed; 2.4m new awards were exceeded by 4m forfeitures/cancellations before vesting or exercises. Carrying annual counts is conservative, not an exact current count.

Uncommenced data-center leases are $288bn at August and purchase obligations total $34.15bn. They are future operating and investment commitments, not added mechanically to current debt. Growth, margin and reinvestment must fund the capacity; contracted revenue can fail to translate into cash if customers default or construction slips.

Net pension liability of $256m is included once and carried from May to August. Matched deferred-compensation investments and liabilities are excluded. Nonmarketable investment carrying amounts of $2.3bn/$2.4bn is a valuation proxy; a 50% haircut changes value by roughly $0.4/share.

FY2017/2018 were retrospectively restated for Topic 606 and pension presentation; FY2016 opening context was not. The transition is excluded from comparable historical growth/capital ranges. History is latest-reported context, not a point-in-time backtest.

Gross uncertain income-tax exposures and related interest/penalties total $13.2bn at May 2026. They are not all assumed immediately payable or deducted as debt; the timing and ultimate settlement remain a material tax sensitivity beyond the normalized 20% operating tax scenario.

Customer prepayment funding reserve is 4,592m for May and 15,955m for August, shown separately from debt and restricted cash. Full, half and omitted reserve scenarios expose a material cash-conversion uncertainty. The reserve is a conservative gross cash-flow accumulation, not a separately reported closing balance.

Fixed claims include NCI, net pension and the separately flagged supplier-financing proxy. Employee option tranches retain 5m vested and 15m expected-to-vest counts; the remaining 1m not-expected-to-vest is conservatively included at an $184.88 inferred strike and a 5-year life.

Option volatility 51% and rate 3.8% use FY2026 grant valuation assumptions as explicit proxies for outstanding claims. Rounded 5m vested and 15m expected-to-vest tranches do not reproduce the 20m subtotal weighted strike exactly. The conservative 1m residual uses strike 184.88 so (5×49.37 + 15×275.90 + 1×184.88) / 21 = 217.63; this is an allocation proxy from rounded values, not a separately reported tranche. Annual remaining lives are carried without aging at August.

Preferred principal is replaced with maximum mandatory-conversion dilution plus separate remaining-dividend PV. Fixed claims include NCI, net pension and the separately flagged supplier-financing proxy. Employee option tranches retain 5m vested and 15m expected-to-vest counts; the remaining 1m not-expected-to-vest is conservatively included at an $184.88 inferred strike and a 5-year life.

The default keeps recent AI buildout intensity in the explicit forecast: sales-to-new-capital of 0.22 means about $4.55 of net reinvestment per $1 of incremental revenue. With current debt and other claims, this scenario produces negative modeled common equity, displayed at a zero floor. It is a conservative conditional scenario, not an assertion that Oracle is worthless. Post-buildout capital efficiency, customer funding and terminal assumptions materially change the result; historical book capital is contextual and is not substituted for future investment.
August 2026 restricted cash of $2,565m is excluded from excess cash. The 141m ATM shares and $19.9bn net proceeds are already in the August balance sheet and are not added again.

Short-term capex financing has no standalone reported closing balance. A conservative claim proxy assumes zero opening at FY2024 and accumulates net financing of $1,422m + $3,345m = $4,767m for May 2026 and subtracts $830m to reach $3,937m for August. The notes-payable schedule reconciles separately and excludes these cash flows. An omitted $1bn opening balance would reduce value by about $0.33/share; the full proxy is about $1.3–1.6/share.

The 31.238285m maximum mandatory preferred-conversion shares are an explicit conservative current-value proxy for a future market-price collar; the minimum 24.99063m sensitivity is available. Preferred carrying amount of $4,954m is not also subtracted. Remaining cumulative dividends are discounted separately at a 6.5% analyst rate; nominal payments provide a sensitivity.

Annual 81m restricted awards and 21m options are carried into August because no complete interim rollforward is disclosed; 2.4m new awards were exceeded by 4m forfeitures/cancellations before vesting or exercises. Carrying annual counts is conservative, not an exact current count.

Uncommenced data-center leases are $288bn at August and purchase obligations total $34.15bn. They are future operating and investment commitments, not added mechanically to current debt. Growth, margin and reinvestment must fund the capacity; contracted revenue can fail to translate into cash if customers default or construction slips.

Net pension liability of $256m is included once and carried from May to August. Matched deferred-compensation investments and liabilities are excluded. Nonmarketable investment carrying amounts of $2.3bn/$2.4bn is a valuation proxy; a 50% haircut changes value by roughly $0.4/share.

FY2017/2018 were retrospectively restated for Topic 606 and pension presentation; FY2016 opening context was not. The transition is excluded from comparable historical growth/capital ranges. History is latest-reported context, not a point-in-time backtest.

Gross uncertain income-tax exposures and related interest/penalties total $13.2bn at May 2026. They are not all assumed immediately payable or deducted as debt; the timing and ultimate settlement remain a material tax sensitivity beyond the normalized 20% operating tax scenario.

Customer prepayment funding reserve is 4,592m for May and 15,955m for August, shown separately from debt and restricted cash. Full, half and omitted reserve scenarios expose a material cash-conversion uncertainty. The reserve is a conservative gross cash-flow accumulation, not a separately reported closing balance.

Option volatility 51% and rate 3.8% use FY2026 grant valuation assumptions as explicit proxies for outstanding claims. Rounded 5m vested and 15m expected-to-vest tranches do not reproduce the 20m subtotal weighted strike exactly. The conservative 1m residual uses strike 184.88 so (5×49.37 + 15×275.90 + 1×184.88) / 21 = 217.63; this is an allocation proxy from rounded values, not a separately reported tranche. Annual remaining lives are carried without aging at August.

Use the filed September 30,2026 balance sheet and nine-month results, filed October 22. TTM is FY 2025 plus 2026 nine months minus 2025 nine months; it is not a provisional earnings-release base.

September cash includes large customer deposits funding future deliveries; not all cash is economically idle. Growth requires substantial inventory, contract assets and manufacturing investment, so the sales-to-capital assumption and cash-reserve sensitivity matter.

September customer-consideration asset 306.500 m is prepaid share-based selling consideration, not surplus cash or an investment. Oracle cashless exercise plus incentive shares 2.154231 m is already in actual common; the old warrant is not charged again. Future amortization reduces revenue and target margins retain customer-incentive costs.

Unconsolidated Fund JV investments are added at carrying value and unfunded capital commitments are deducted. Fund JV debt is nonrecourse and not consolidated; deferred intra-entity profit is an accounting elimination, not a second cash debt. Consolidated Korean JV debt and minority interest remain in the bridge.

Supplier commitments of 5.8 bn over multiple years support planned production and are not added wholesale as debt; inventory and equipment purchases belong in forecast reinvestment. Customer concentration, performance guarantees and demand shortfalls can materially change the outcome.

Capped-call coverage 33.549508 m uses the annual disclosed contract carried forward because the September filing refers to the same terms and discloses no termination. It is a separate derivative even though the 2028 notes are now redeemed; omit-hedge sensitivity tests this residual uncertainty.

Reserve the full reported customer-deposit balance as conservative operating funding:78.207 m annual and 661.354 m September. These are deposits from Note 3 contract balances, separate from deferred revenue 65.608 m/93.026 m; they are neither legally restricted cash nor an additional debt claim. Gross deposits may exceed remaining cash fulfillment costs. The 1.5 x sales-to-capital assumption funds gross incremental operating investment without assuming repeat customer-advance funding; full, half and no reserve sensitivities show the uncertainty.

Reported debt retains all book financing obligations. A conservative carrying-value stress adds back 200.511 m annual/149.301 m September to model debt, instead of assuming the noncash financing residual offsets Energy Server assets at expiry. This changes only the valuation bridge; original filings remain intact.

Starting operating income excludes own-share product profit on sales to unconsolidated affiliates that the filing eliminates below EBIT; raw GAAP figures remain visible. TTM uses the rounded 16.9 m current-period elimination.

Annual Oracle warrant uses disclosed terms; September has no remaining warrant claim because settlement shares are already outstanding.

Intrinsic convertible/capped-call allocation omits full time value, discounting and counterparty risk. Make-whole conversion increments apply only to specified events and are excluded from ordinary continuation; all-series principal/conversion and omitted/maximal hedge sensitivities bound useful alternatives.

Reported RSU/PSU counts are assumed to vest. Conditional performance multipliers beyond disclosed outstanding units and ungranted share-pool capacity are excluded. Existing EPP derivative liability and unfunded JV commitments are deducted once at reported amounts; no new investment value is assumed for the commitments.

Use the filed September 30,2026 balance sheet and nine-month results, filed October 22. TTM is FY 2025 plus 2026 nine months minus 2025 nine months; it is not a provisional earnings-release base.

September cash includes large customer deposits funding future deliveries; not all cash is economically idle. Growth requires substantial inventory, contract assets and manufacturing investment, so the sales-to-capital assumption and cash-reserve sensitivity matter.

September customer-consideration asset 306.500 m is prepaid share-based selling consideration, not surplus cash or an investment. Oracle cashless exercise plus incentive shares 2.154231 m is already in actual common; the old warrant is not charged again. Future amortization reduces revenue and target margins retain customer-incentive costs.

Unconsolidated Fund JV investments are added at carrying value and unfunded capital commitments are deducted. Fund JV debt is nonrecourse and not consolidated; deferred intra-entity profit is an accounting elimination, not a second cash debt. Consolidated Korean JV debt and minority interest remain in the bridge.

Supplier commitments of 5.8 bn over multiple years support planned production and are not added wholesale as debt; inventory and equipment purchases belong in forecast reinvestment. Customer concentration, performance guarantees and demand shortfalls can materially change the outcome.

Capped-call coverage 33.549508 m uses the annual disclosed contract carried forward because the September filing refers to the same terms and discloses no termination. It is a separate derivative even though the 2028 notes are now redeemed; omit-hedge sensitivity tests this residual uncertainty.

Reserve the full reported customer-deposit balance as conservative operating funding:78.207 m annual and 661.354 m September. These are deposits from Note 3 contract balances, separate from deferred revenue 65.608 m/93.026 m; they are neither legally restricted cash nor an additional debt claim. Gross deposits may exceed remaining cash fulfillment costs. The 1.5 x sales-to-capital assumption funds gross incremental operating investment without assuming repeat customer-advance funding; full, half and no reserve sensitivities show the uncertainty.

Reported debt retains all book financing obligations. A conservative carrying-value stress adds back 200.511 m annual/149.301 m September to model debt, instead of assuming the noncash financing residual offsets Energy Server assets at expiry. This changes only the valuation bridge; original filings remain intact.

Intrinsic convertible/capped-call allocation omits full time value, discounting and counterparty risk.
